## **1. Load Data and Create Phyloseq Object**

```{r libraries, include=FALSE}
library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(vegan)
library(ggtext)
```


```{r load-data,message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(42)

# Load CSV files
otu_table <- read.csv("otu_table_mycoinferno.csv", row.names = 1)
taxonomy_table <- read.csv("tax_table_mycoinferno.csv", row.names = 1)
metadata <- read.csv("metadata.csv", row.names = 1)

# Clean factor levels
metadata$burn_severity <- factor(
  metadata$burn_severity,
  levels = c("High", "Low_New", "Low_Old", "Never"),
  labels = c("High", "Low (Initial)", "Low (Advanced)", "Suppressed")
)

table(metadata$burn_severity, useNA = "ifany")

# Convert to phyloseq components
OTU <- otu_table(as.matrix(otu_table), taxa_are_rows = TRUE)
TAX <- tax_table(as.matrix(taxonomy_table))
META <- sample_data(metadata)

# Create phyloseq object
physeq <- phyloseq(OTU, TAX, META)
```


## **2. Filter and Transform**
```{r filter-and-transform}

# ============================================================
# A. ALL-TAXA DATASET
# ============================================================

# Exclude samples that produce a degenerate all-taxa NMDS
problematic_samples_full <- c(
  "Seedling248",
  "Seedling243"
)

physeq_filtered_full <- phyloseq::prune_samples(
  !phyloseq::sample_names(physeq) %in% problematic_samples_full,
  physeq
)

# Convert counts within each sample to relative abundance
physeq_all_transformed <- phyloseq::transform_sample_counts(
  physeq_filtered_full,
  function(x) {
    if (sum(x) == 0) {
      rep(0, length(x))
    } else {
      x / sum(x)
    }
  }
)


# ============================================================
# B. EcM-ONLY DATASET
# ============================================================

# Start from the complete original phyloseq object.
# Non-EcM OTUs are removed first, after which samples with
# no remaining EcM observations are removed automatically.

physeq_emf_unfiltered <- physeq


# -----------------------------
# Define non-EcM OTUs
# -----------------------------

# Names below exactly match fungal_taxon / taxa_names()
# in the current OTU table.

non_emf_taxa <- c(
  "Exophiala_equina",
  "Phialocephala_fortinii",
  "Phialocephala_sp",
  "Phialocephala_helvetica",
  "Phialomyces_arenicola",
  "Entoloma_sp",
  "Paraphoma_fimeti",
  "Eurotiales_sp",
  "Ilyonectria_sp",
  "Ilyonectria_destructans",
  "Helotiales_sp",
  "Leohumicola_minima",
  "Leohumicola_sp",
  "Myxomphalia_maura",
  "Helotiaceae",
  "Nectriaceae",
  "Pyronema_sp"
)


# -----------------------------
# Identify non-EcM OTUs
# -----------------------------

non_emf_otus <- phyloseq::taxa_names(
  physeq_emf_unfiltered
)[
  phyloseq::taxa_names(physeq_emf_unfiltered) %in%
    non_emf_taxa
]


# -----------------------------
# Audit matching BEFORE filtering
# -----------------------------

cat("\nNon-EcM OTUs identified for removal:\n")
print(non_emf_otus)

cat(
  "\nNumber of non-EcM OTUs identified:",
  length(non_emf_otus),
  "\n"
)

# Every OTU in the removal list should exist in the current OTU table.
unmatched_non_emf <- setdiff(
  non_emf_taxa,
  phyloseq::taxa_names(physeq_emf_unfiltered)
)

cat("\nNon-EcM taxa that failed to match an OTU name:\n")
print(unmatched_non_emf)

# HARD STOP if any intended removal fails to match.
stopifnot(length(unmatched_non_emf) == 0)

# HARD STOP if the removal vector somehow matches nothing.
stopifnot(length(non_emf_otus) > 0)


# -----------------------------
# Remove non-EcM OTUs
# -----------------------------

n_otus_before <- phyloseq::ntaxa(
  physeq_emf_unfiltered
)

physeq_emf <- phyloseq::prune_taxa(
  !phyloseq::taxa_names(physeq_emf_unfiltered) %in%
    non_emf_otus,
  physeq_emf_unfiltered
)

n_otus_after <- phyloseq::ntaxa(
  physeq_emf
)

removed_non_emf_otus <- setdiff(
  phyloseq::taxa_names(physeq_emf_unfiltered),
  phyloseq::taxa_names(physeq_emf)
)

cat("\nOTUs before EcM filtering:", n_otus_before, "\n")
cat("OTUs after EcM filtering:", n_otus_after, "\n")

cat("\nOTUs actually removed:\n")
print(removed_non_emf_otus)


# -----------------------------
# Hard checks on OTU filtering
# -----------------------------

# The OTUs actually removed must exactly equal
# the OTUs designated as non-EcM.
stopifnot(
  setequal(
    removed_non_emf_otus,
    non_emf_otus
  )
)

# No designated non-EcM OTU may remain.
stopifnot(
  !any(
    phyloseq::taxa_names(physeq_emf) %in%
      non_emf_taxa
  )
)


# -----------------------------
# Remove samples with zero
# remaining EcM observations
# -----------------------------

samples_before_zero_pruning <- phyloseq::sample_names(
  physeq_emf
)

physeq_emf <- phyloseq::prune_samples(
  phyloseq::sample_sums(physeq_emf) > 0,
  physeq_emf
)

samples_after_zero_pruning <- phyloseq::sample_names(
  physeq_emf
)

zero_emf_samples <- setdiff(
  samples_before_zero_pruning,
  samples_after_zero_pruning
)

cat(
  "\nSamples removed because no EcM observations remained:\n"
)
print(zero_emf_samples)


# -----------------------------
# Verify known zero-EcM samples
# -----------------------------

focal_emf_check <- c(
  Seedling243 = "Seedling243" %in%
    phyloseq::sample_names(physeq_emf),

  Seedling248 = "Seedling248" %in%
    phyloseq::sample_names(physeq_emf),

  Seedling269 = "Seedling269" %in%
    phyloseq::sample_names(physeq_emf)
)

cat("\nFocal-sample retention after EcM filtering:\n")
print(focal_emf_check)

# All three should be absent from the EcM dataset.
stopifnot(
  all(focal_emf_check == FALSE)
)


# -----------------------------
# Transform EcM counts to
# relative abundance
# -----------------------------

physeq_emf_transformed <- phyloseq::transform_sample_counts(
  physeq_emf,
  function(x) {
    if (sum(x) == 0) {
      rep(0, length(x))
    } else {
      x / sum(x)
    }
  }
)


# -----------------------------
# Final EcM-object audit
# -----------------------------

cat(
  "\nFinal EcM dataset:",
  phyloseq::nsamples(physeq_emf_transformed),
  "samples and",
  phyloseq::ntaxa(physeq_emf_transformed),
  "OTUs\n"
)

# No zero-sum samples should remain.
stopifnot(
  all(
    phyloseq::sample_sums(
      physeq_emf_transformed
    ) > 0
  )
)

# No designated non-EcM OTUs should remain.
stopifnot(
  !any(
    phyloseq::taxa_names(
      physeq_emf_transformed
    ) %in%
      non_emf_taxa
  )
)
```

## **3. Ordinate and Plot (w/ post-review diagnostics/changes**
```{r ordinate and plot, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}

# Run NMDS ordinations
set.seed(42)

nmds_all <- phyloseq::ordinate(
  physeq_all_transformed,
  method = "NMDS",
  distance = "bray",
  trymax = 200
)

set.seed(42)

nmds_emf <- phyloseq::ordinate(
  physeq_emf_transformed,
  method = "NMDS",
  distance = "bray",
  trymax = 200
)


# Fit EcM taxa vectors to NMDS

# Extract EcM OTU matrix
emf_otu <- as(
  phyloseq::otu_table(physeq_emf_transformed),
  "matrix"
)

# Make samples rows and OTUs columns
if (phyloseq::taxa_are_rows(physeq_emf_transformed)) {
  emf_otu <- t(emf_otu)
}

# Ensure sample order matches the NMDS
emf_otu <- emf_otu[
  rownames(vegan::scores(nmds_emf, display = "sites")),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Fit OTUs to ordination
set.seed(42)

emf_vectors <- vegan::envfit(
  nmds_emf,
  emf_otu,
  permutations = 9999
)

print(emf_vectors)

# Fit genus-level EcM vectors to existing OTU-level NMDS


# Extract EcM abundance matrix
emf_otu <- as(
  phyloseq::otu_table(physeq_emf_transformed),
  "matrix"
)

# Make samples rows and OTUs columns
if (phyloseq::taxa_are_rows(physeq_emf_transformed)) {
  emf_otu <- t(emf_otu)
}

# Get taxonomy table for retained EcM OTUs
emf_tax <- as(
  phyloseq::tax_table(physeq_emf_transformed),
  "matrix"
)

# Match taxonomy order to OTU columns
emf_tax <- emf_tax[
  colnames(emf_otu),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Inspect genus names before aggregation
print(
  unique(emf_tax[, "genus"])
)

# Replace blank genus entries with the OTU name
# so higher-level identifications are not accidentally combined
genus_names <- emf_tax[, "genus"]

blank_genus <- is.na(genus_names) | genus_names == ""

genus_names[blank_genus] <- colnames(emf_otu)[blank_genus]

#Reclassify C. finlandica to Hyaloscypha for genus-level analysis
genus_names[
  colnames(emf_otu) == "Cadophora_finlandica"
] <- "Hyaloscypha"


# Check assignments
print(
  data.frame(
    OTU = colnames(emf_otu),
    genus_for_envfit = genus_names
  )
)

# Aggregate OTU abundances by genus
emf_genus <- sapply(
  unique(genus_names),
  function(g) {
    rowSums(
      emf_otu[
        ,
        genus_names == g,
        drop = FALSE
      ]
    )
  }
)

# Ensure matrix format
emf_genus <- as.matrix(emf_genus)

# Align sample order with NMDS
emf_genus <- emf_genus[
  rownames(vegan::scores(nmds_emf, display = "sites")),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Fit genus vectors to the existing EcM NMDS
set.seed(42)

emf_genus_vectors <- vegan::envfit(
  nmds_emf,
  emf_genus,
  permutations = 9999
)

print(emf_genus_vectors)

# Extract vector coordinates
genus_vector_scores <- as.data.frame(
  vegan::scores(
    emf_genus_vectors,
    display = "vectors"
  )
)

# Add genus names
genus_vector_scores$Genus <- rownames(genus_vector_scores)

# Extract r-squared and raw permutation p-values
genus_vector_scores$R2 <- emf_genus_vectors$vectors$r
genus_vector_scores$p_raw <- emf_genus_vectors$vectors$pvals

# FDR correction
genus_vector_scores$p_FDR <- p.adjust(
  genus_vector_scores$p_raw,
  method = "BH"
)

# Reorder columns
genus_vector_table <- genus_vector_scores[
  ,
  c(
    "Genus",
    "NMDS1",
    "NMDS2",
    "R2",
    "p_raw",
    "p_FDR"
  )
]

# Sort by strongest association
genus_vector_table <- genus_vector_table[
  order(genus_vector_table$R2, decreasing = TRUE),
]

print(genus_vector_table)

# Prepare significant genus vectors for EMF NMDS plot

# Keep only genera significant after FDR correction
emf_genus_vectors_plot <- genus_vector_table[
  genus_vector_table$p_FDR < 0.05,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Check which genera will be plotted
print(emf_genus_vectors_plot)

# Scale arrows for visibility on the NMDS
# Start with 3
vector_multiplier <- 3

emf_genus_vectors_plot$NMDS1_plot <-
  emf_genus_vectors_plot$NMDS1 * vector_multiplier

emf_genus_vectors_plot$NMDS2_plot <-
  emf_genus_vectors_plot$NMDS2 * vector_multiplier

# -----------------------------
# Manual label offsets for EcM vectors
# -----------------------------

emf_genus_vectors_plot$label_nudge_x <- c(
  Sebacina    = -0.15,
  Rhizopogon  =  0.10,
  Pustularia  = -0.10
)[emf_genus_vectors_plot$Genus]

emf_genus_vectors_plot$label_nudge_y <- c(
  Sebacina    =  0.15,
  Rhizopogon  =  0.15,
  Pustularia  = -0.10
)[emf_genus_vectors_plot$Genus]

emf_genus_vectors_plot$label_x <-
  emf_genus_vectors_plot$NMDS1_plot +
  emf_genus_vectors_plot$label_nudge_x

emf_genus_vectors_plot$label_y <-
  emf_genus_vectors_plot$NMDS2_plot +
  emf_genus_vectors_plot$label_nudge_y

# ============================================================
# Fit genus-level ALL-TAXA vectors to existing all-taxa NMDS
# ============================================================

# Extract all-taxa abundance matrix
all_otu <- as(
  phyloseq::otu_table(physeq_all_transformed),
  "matrix"
)

# Make samples rows and OTUs columns
if (phyloseq::taxa_are_rows(physeq_all_transformed)) {
  all_otu <- t(all_otu)
}

# Match sample order to NMDS
all_otu <- all_otu[
  rownames(vegan::scores(nmds_all, display = "sites")),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]


# -----------------------------
# Get taxonomy information
# -----------------------------

all_tax <- as(
  phyloseq::tax_table(physeq_all_transformed),
  "matrix"
)

# Match taxonomy order to OTU columns
all_tax <- all_tax[
  colnames(all_otu),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Get genus assignments
all_genus_names <- all_tax[, "genus"]

# If genus is blank, retain the OTU name rather than
# accidentally grouping unrelated higher-level taxa
blank_all_genus <-
  is.na(all_genus_names) | all_genus_names == ""

all_genus_names[blank_all_genus] <-
  colnames(all_otu)[blank_all_genus]


# -----------------------------
# Taxonomic synonym correction
# for genus-level analysis only
# -----------------------------

# Cadophora finlandica is treated as Hyaloscypha
all_genus_names[
  colnames(all_otu) == "Cadophora_finlandica"
] <- "Hyaloscypha"


# Check genus assignments
print(
  data.frame(
    OTU = colnames(all_otu),
    genus_for_envfit = all_genus_names
  )
)


# -----------------------------
# Aggregate abundances by genus
# -----------------------------

all_genus <- sapply(
  unique(all_genus_names),
  function(g) {
    rowSums(
      all_otu[
        ,
        all_genus_names == g,
        drop = FALSE
      ]
    )
  }
)

all_genus <- as.matrix(all_genus)

# Ensure sample order still matches NMDS
all_genus <- all_genus[
  rownames(vegan::scores(nmds_all, display = "sites")),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]


# -----------------------------
# Fit genus vectors
# -----------------------------

set.seed(42)

all_genus_vectors <- vegan::envfit(
  nmds_all,
  all_genus,
  permutations = 9999
)

print(all_genus_vectors)


# -----------------------------
# Extract vector results
# -----------------------------

all_genus_vector_scores <- as.data.frame(
  vegan::scores(
    all_genus_vectors,
    display = "vectors"
  )
)

all_genus_vector_scores$Genus <-
  rownames(all_genus_vector_scores)

all_genus_vector_scores$R2 <-
  all_genus_vectors$vectors$r

all_genus_vector_scores$p_raw <-
  all_genus_vectors$vectors$pvals

# FDR correction
all_genus_vector_scores$p_FDR <- p.adjust(
  all_genus_vector_scores$p_raw,
  method = "BH"
)

# Create results table
all_genus_vector_table <- all_genus_vector_scores[
  ,
  c(
    "Genus",
    "NMDS1",
    "NMDS2",
    "R2",
    "p_raw",
    "p_FDR"
  )
]

# Sort strongest associations first
all_genus_vector_table <- all_genus_vector_table[
  order(
    all_genus_vector_table$R2,
    decreasing = TRUE
  ),
]

print(all_genus_vector_table)


# -----------------------------
# Keep only significant genera
# after FDR correction
# -----------------------------

all_genus_vectors_plot <- all_genus_vector_table[
  all_genus_vector_table$p_FDR < 0.05,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

print(all_genus_vectors_plot)


# -----------------------------
# Scale vectors for plotting
# -----------------------------

all_vector_multiplier <- 3

# IMPORTANT:
# My plotted all-taxa NMDS reverses BOTH NMDS1 and NMDS2.
# Therefore the vectors must be reversed on BOTH axes too.
# This seems unnecessary, but not having it kept messing up the 
# orientation of the centroids.

all_genus_vectors_plot$NMDS1_plot <-
  -all_genus_vectors_plot$NMDS1 *
  all_vector_multiplier

all_genus_vectors_plot$NMDS2_plot <-
  -all_genus_vectors_plot$NMDS2 *
  all_vector_multiplier

# -----------------------------
# Manual label offsets for all-taxa vectors
# -----------------------------

all_genus_vectors_plot$label_nudge_x <- c(
  Ilyonectria = -0.15,
  Rhizopogon  =  0.10,
  Pustularia  =  0.00,
  Leohumicola = -0.15
)[all_genus_vectors_plot$Genus]

all_genus_vectors_plot$label_nudge_y <- c(
  Ilyonectria =  0.10,
  Rhizopogon  =  0.10,
  Pustularia  = -0.10,
  Leohumicola = -0.10
)[all_genus_vectors_plot$Genus]

all_genus_vectors_plot$label_x <-
  all_genus_vectors_plot$NMDS1_plot +
  all_genus_vectors_plot$label_nudge_x

all_genus_vectors_plot$label_y <-
  all_genus_vectors_plot$NMDS2_plot +
  all_genus_vectors_plot$label_nudge_y

# Convert ordination output to data frames with metadata merged in
ordination_df_all <- as.data.frame(scores(nmds_all, display = "sites"))
ordination_df_all$sample <- rownames(ordination_df_all)
ordination_df_all <- merge(ordination_df_all, as.data.frame(sample_data(physeq_all_transformed)), by.x = "sample", by.y = "row.names")

ordination_df_emf <- as.data.frame(scores(nmds_emf, display = "sites"))
ordination_df_emf$sample <- rownames(ordination_df_emf)
ordination_df_emf <- merge(ordination_df_emf, as.data.frame(sample_data(physeq_emf_transformed)), by.x = "sample", by.y = "row.names")

# ============================================================
# DIAGNOSTIC: What taxa characterize positive NMDS2?
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)


# 1. Rank EMF samples from highest to lowest NMDS2


nmds2_ranked <- ordination_df_emf %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(NMDS2)) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    sample,
    burn_severity,
    water,
    NMDS1,
    NMDS2
  )

print(nmds2_ranked)



# 2. Look at the uppermost samples
#
# Start with the 10 samples having the highest NMDS2 scores.
# This is diagnostic only


upper_samples <- nmds2_ranked %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 10)

print(upper_samples)



# 3. Extract EMF abundances for those samples


upper_sample_names <- upper_samples$sample

upper_emf <- emf_otu[
  upper_sample_names,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]



# 4. Total abundance of each EMF OTU in the upper samples


upper_taxa <- data.frame(
  Taxon = colnames(upper_emf),
  Upper_total = colSums(upper_emf)
)

upper_taxa <- upper_taxa %>%
  dplyr::filter(Upper_total > 0) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(Upper_total))

print(upper_taxa)



# 5. Compare upper samples with all remaining EMF samples


remaining_sample_names <- setdiff(
  rownames(emf_otu),
  upper_sample_names
)

remaining_emf <- emf_otu[
  remaining_sample_names,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

taxon_comparison <- data.frame(
  Taxon = colnames(emf_otu),

  Upper_total = colSums(
    emf_otu[upper_sample_names, , drop = FALSE]
  ),

  Other_total = colSums(
    remaining_emf
  ),

  Upper_prevalence = colSums(
    emf_otu[upper_sample_names, , drop = FALSE] > 0
  ),

  Other_prevalence = colSums(
    remaining_emf > 0
  )
)


# 6. Convert prevalence to proportions because the two
# groups contain different numbers of seedlings

taxon_comparison <- taxon_comparison %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Upper_prevalence_prop =
      Upper_prevalence / length(upper_sample_names),

    Other_prevalence_prop =
      Other_prevalence / length(remaining_sample_names),

    Prevalence_difference =
      Upper_prevalence_prop - Other_prevalence_prop
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Upper_total > 0 | Other_total > 0
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    desc(Prevalence_difference)
  )

print(taxon_comparison)

#----------------------------
# NOW BUILD THE ACTUAL PLOT
#----------------------------

# Colors
burn_colors_cb <- c(
  "High"       = hcl(15,  75, 55),
  "Low (Initial)"  = hcl(260, 60, 65),
  "Low (Advanced)"  = hcl(75,  65, 75),
  "Suppressed"      = hcl(330, 50, 70)
)

lims_x <- c(-4, 3)
lims_y <- c(-3, 2)
annotation_x <- 0.55
annotation_y <- -2.75

# Flip coordinates ONCE so both match direction

ordination_df_emf$NMDS1 <- -ordination_df_emf$NMDS1
ordination_df_all$NMDS2 <- -ordination_df_all$NMDS2


# Flip NMDS1 for horizontal alignment
ordination_df_all$NMDS1 <- -ordination_df_all$NMDS1
ordination_df_emf$NMDS1 <- -ordination_df_emf$NMDS1

# Fix factor levels
ordination_df_all$burn_severity <- factor(trimws(ordination_df_all$burn_severity),
  levels = c("High", "Low (Initial)", "Low (Advanced)", "Suppressed"))
ordination_df_emf$burn_severity <- factor(trimws(ordination_df_emf$burn_severity),
  levels = c("High", "Low (Initial)", "Low (Advanced)", "Suppressed"))

# Standardize water-treatment labels for both NMDS plots
ordination_df_all$water <- factor(
  dplyr::recode(
    trimws(ordination_df_all$water),
    "Drought" = "Water Limitation",
    "Normal" = "Full Water"
  ),
  levels = c("Water Limitation", "Full Water")
)

ordination_df_emf$water <- factor(
  dplyr::recode(
    trimws(ordination_df_emf$water),
    "Drought" = "Water Limitation",
    "Normal" = "Full Water"
  ),
  levels = c("Water Limitation", "Full Water")
)


# PLOT A: All Taxa

p_all <- ggplot(
  ordination_df_all,
  aes(
    NMDS1,
    NMDS2,
    color = burn_severity,
    shape = water
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +

  # Genus vectors
  geom_segment(
    data = all_genus_vectors_plot,
    aes(
      x = 0,
      y = 0,
      xend = NMDS1_plot,
      yend = NMDS2_plot
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.7,
    arrow = grid::arrow(
      length = grid::unit(0.18, "cm")
    )
  ) +

  # Genus labels
  geom_text(
  data = all_genus_vectors_plot,
  aes(
    x = label_x,
    y = label_y,
    label = Genus
  ),
  inherit.aes = FALSE,
  color = "black",
  fontface = "italic",
  size = 4.5
) +

  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Fire History",
    values = burn_colors_cb
  ) +

  scale_shape_manual(
    name = "Water Treatment",
    values = c(
```

# **6. Pairwise PERMANOVA by Burn Treatment**

```{r}
pairwise_permanova <- function(
    physeq_object,
    group_var = "burn_severity",
    permutations = 9999,
    p_adjust_method = "holm") {

  # Extract metadata
  sample_df <- as(
    phyloseq::sample_data(physeq_object),
    "data.frame"
  )

  # Drop unused treatment levels
  sample_df[[group_var]] <- droplevels(
  as.factor(sample_df[[group_var]])
)

  groups <- levels(
    sample_df[[group_var]]
  )

  comparisons <- combn(
    groups,
    2,
    simplify = FALSE
  )

  results <- lapply(
    comparisons,
    function(pair) {

      # Identify samples belonging to the two treatments
      samples_to_keep <- rownames(sample_df)[
        sample_df[[group_var]] %in% pair
      ]

      # Subset phyloseq object
      ps_pair <- phyloseq::prune_samples(
        phyloseq::sample_names(physeq_object) %in%
          samples_to_keep,
        physeq_object
      )

      # Remove taxa absent from this pair
      ps_pair <- phyloseq::prune_taxa(
        phyloseq::taxa_sums(ps_pair) > 0,
        ps_pair
      )

      # Recalculate Bray-Curtis for this pair
      pair_dist <- phyloseq::distance(
        ps_pair,
        method = "bray"
      )

      # Extract metadata
      pair_metadata <- as(
        phyloseq::sample_data(ps_pair),
        "data.frame"
      )

      # Align metadata with distance matrix
      pair_metadata <- pair_metadata[
        labels(pair_dist),
        ,
        drop = FALSE
      ]

      pair_metadata[[group_var]] <- droplevels(
  as.factor(pair_metadata[[group_var]])
)

      # Confirm alignment
      stopifnot(
        identical(
          rownames(pair_metadata),
          labels(pair_dist)
        )
      )

      # Construct formula from group_var
      pair_formula <- stats::as.formula(
        paste("pair_dist ~", group_var)
      )

      # Pairwise PERMANOVA
      set.seed(42)

      model <- vegan::adonis2(
        pair_formula,
        data = pair_metadata,
        permutations = permutations
      )

      data.frame(
        Group_1 = pair[1],
        Group_2 = pair[2],
        n_1 = sum(
          pair_metadata[[group_var]] == pair[1]
        ),
        n_2 = sum(
          pair_metadata[[group_var]] == pair[2]
        ),
        R2 = model$R2[1],
        F = model$F[1],
        p_raw = model$`Pr(>F)`[1]
      )
    }
  )

  results <- do.call(
    rbind,
    results
  )

  # Holm correction across the six pairwise comparisons
  results$p_adjusted <- p.adjust(
    results$p_raw,
    method = p_adjust_method
  )

  results$significant <-
    results$p_adjusted < 0.05

  results
}


# -----------------------------
# All fungal taxa
# -----------------------------

pairwise_all <- pairwise_permanova(
  physeq_all_transformed,
  permutations = 9999,
  p_adjust_method = "holm"
)

print(pairwise_all)


# -----------------------------
# EcM taxa only
# -----------------------------

pairwise_emf <- pairwise_permanova(
  physeq_emf_transformed,
  permutations = 9999,
  p_adjust_method = "holm"
)

print(pairwise_emf)

```


# **7. Exploratory NMDS Diagnostics**
# This section does NOT modify objects used in the primary analysis.
# It reconstructs an all-sample dataset solely to investigate why
# Seedling243, Seedling248, and Seedling269 affect NMDS behavior.

```{r exploratory-nmds-diagnostics}

# -----------------------------
# A. Recreate an ALL-SAMPLE transformed object
# -----------------------------

# Start from the original phyloseq object so no currently excluded
# samples are removed.
physeq_all_samples_transformed <- phyloseq::transform_sample_counts(
  physeq,
  function(x) {
    if (sum(x) == 0) rep(0, length(x)) else x / sum(x)
  }
)

# Problem samples of interest
problem_samples <- c(
  "Seedling243",
  "Seedling248",
  "Seedling269"
)

# Confirm that all three are present
problem_samples %in% sample_names(physeq_all_samples_transformed)


# -----------------------------
# B. Calculate Bray-Curtis matrix
# with ALL samples retained
# -----------------------------

bray_all_samples <- phyloseq::distance(
  physeq_all_samples_transformed,
  method = "bray"
)

bray_matrix_all <- as.matrix(bray_all_samples)

# Check dimensions
dim(bray_matrix_all)


# -----------------------------
# C. Inspect distances involving
# the three suspect samples
# -----------------------------

problem_distance_matrix <- bray_matrix_all[
  problem_samples,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

print(problem_distance_matrix)


# -----------------------------
# D. Mean and median dissimilarity
# of every sample to all others
# -----------------------------

# Replace diagonal zero with NA so samples are not compared with themselves
bray_no_diag <- bray_matrix_all
diag(bray_no_diag) <- NA

mean_dissimilarity <- rowMeans(
  bray_no_diag,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

median_dissimilarity <- apply(
  bray_no_diag,
  1,
  median,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

dissimilarity_summary <- data.frame(
  sample = names(mean_dissimilarity),
  mean_bray = mean_dissimilarity,
  median_bray = median_dissimilarity
)

# Sort most isolated samples first
dissimilarity_summary <- dissimilarity_summary[
  order(dissimilarity_summary$mean_bray, decreasing = TRUE),
]

print(dissimilarity_summary)


# -----------------------------
# E. Count Bray-Curtis = 1.0
# distances for each sample
# -----------------------------

max_distance_counts <- rowSums(
  bray_matrix_all == 1
)

max_distance_summary <- data.frame(
  sample = names(max_distance_counts),
  n_distances_equal_1 = max_distance_counts
)

max_distance_summary <- max_distance_summary[
  order(
    max_distance_summary$n_distances_equal_1,
    decreasing = TRUE
  ),
]

print(max_distance_summary)


# -----------------------------
# F. Nearest and farthest neighbors
# of suspect samples
# -----------------------------

for (s in problem_samples) {

  x <- bray_matrix_all[s, ]

  # Remove self-comparison
  x <- x[names(x) != s]

  cat("\n\n====================\n")
  cat("Sample:", s, "\n")
  cat("====================\n")

  cat("\nNearest neighbors:\n")
  print(head(sort(x), 10))

  cat("\nFarthest neighbors:\n")
  print(head(sort(x, decreasing = TRUE), 10))
}


# -----------------------------
# G. Distances among the three
# problem samples themselves
# -----------------------------

problem_to_problem <- bray_matrix_all[
  problem_samples,
  problem_samples,
  drop = FALSE
]

print(problem_to_problem)


# -----------------------------
# H. Compare suspect samples with
# the rest of the dataset
# -----------------------------

problem_summary <- dissimilarity_summary[
  dissimilarity_summary$sample %in% problem_samples,
]

print(problem_summary)

problem_maxdist_summary <- max_distance_summary[
  max_distance_summary$sample %in% problem_samples,
]

print(problem_maxdist_summary)
```

```{r}
  emf_metadata_sensitivity$burn_severity
)

# ANOVA-style test
print(
  anova(bd_emf_sensitivity)
)

# Permutation test
set.seed(42)

print(
  vegan::permutest(
    bd_emf_sensitivity,
    permutations = 9999
  )
)


# ============================================================
# Pairwise PERMANOVA: EMF
# ============================================================

set.seed(42)

pairwise_emf_sensitivity <- pairwise_permanova(
  physeq_emf_sensitivity_transformed,
  permutations = 9999,
  p_adjust_method = "holm"
)

print(pairwise_emf_sensitivity)
```


# ============================================================
# Small diagnostic:
# Identify High-severity samples closest to the
# Low (Initial) centroid in EcM NMDS space
# ============================================================
```{r}

library(dplyr)

# Calculate centroid of Low (Initial) samples
low_initial_centroid <- ordination_df_emf %>%
  dplyr::filter(burn_severity == "Low (Initial)") %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    centroid_NMDS1 = mean(NMDS1),
    centroid_NMDS2 = mean(NMDS2)
  )

print(low_initial_centroid)

# Calculate distance of each High sample from that centroid
high_to_low_initial <- ordination_df_emf %>%
  dplyr::filter(burn_severity == "High") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    distance_to_low_initial_centroid = sqrt(
      (NMDS1 - low_initial_centroid$centroid_NMDS1)^2 +
      (NMDS2 - low_initial_centroid$centroid_NMDS2)^2
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(distance_to_low_initial_centroid)

# Show High samples from closest to farthest
print(
  high_to_low_initial %>%
    dplyr::select(
      sample,
      NMDS1,
      NMDS2,
      distance_to_low_initial_centroid
    )
)

# Just the two closest
closest_two_high <- high_to_low_initial %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 2)

print(closest_two_high$sample)
```
